desks.Dividends: Apple goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter, unchanged, payable Nov 16; the last day to buy for the dividend is the close of Wed Nov 11. Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the first payment at the raised rate and its 24th consecutive annual increase, payable Dec 10. Nasdaq's indicated annual dividend for Microsoft still shows the stale $3.64; the correct annualized rate at $0.98 per quarter is $3.92. Nvidia has not yet declared its December dividend; the historical pattern points to a late-November declaration. SPY and QQQ December distributions fall outside the window. Tesla pays no dividend. Apple and Microsoft yields are UNVERIFIED against a live price pull.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus EPS of $2.49 (Nasdaq, 13 estimates). Options imply a move of about 9.6% (Nov 18 at-the-money straddle $17.18 on a $178.67 underlying), about 1.7 times the 5.8% average absolute reaction of the last three prints. Nvidia beat consensus all three times yet fell the next session twice. The stock is down 13.6% in four sessions ($206.69 on Nov 3 to $178.67 today). The Nov 17 print now carries a governance overhang: the board announced Sun Nov 8 an independent investigation, with outside counsel, into reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; the company states no reason to believe secrets were compromised. The investigation outcome and timeline are UNVERIFIED.
desks.Futures: USDA WASDE and Crop Production report Tue Nov 10, 12:00 ET. Soybeans are the wildcard: the ending-stocks survey spread is 280-404 million bushels, 39% of the prior estimate. The EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report is Thu Nov 12, 12:00 ET, not Wed Nov 11, a Veterans Day delay. Crude fell 3-4% Mon on the diplomacy headline (Trump told CNN renewed US attacks on Iran are 'highly unlikely' if Tehran progresses toward a nuclear agreement and reopening Hormuz), but physical Hormuz shipping has not normalized: a UKMTO-verified tanker fire and projectile strike Nov 7, a Houthi hit damaging the Aramco Tower Nov 8, and an attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline Nov 9 (operations unaffected). OPEC+ holds December output at September required levels; next meeting Nov 29. US-Ukraine-Russia talks restart Tue Nov 11 in Abu Dhabi.
desks.Parity: No new SPX, SPY, or QQQ methodology change was found in the last few days, and no published put-call or box parity violation was found for this week. S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Oct 23 a growth/value classification change effective before the open Mon Dec 21 (pro-forma files Dec 4): growth drops 12-month price momentum; value adds free-cash-flow-to-price and an intangibles-adjusted book-to-price. It is a style-index reconstitution only, with no change to S&P 500 membership, weighting, or SPX option mechanics, so no parity implication. CBOE complex-order filing SR-CBOE-2026-081 (filed Oct 9) is execution plumbing for multi-leg orders, not a parity change. No parity check of the Nov 5 crash session has been published; absence of a report is not proof parity held. The current live SPX box-spread rate is UNVERIFIED.
desks.Premium: All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT. The Nov 5 crash day still drives 46-63% of each 20-day realized-variance window (SPY 62.6%, AAPL 55.8%, TSLA 51.3%). Front IV sits below the jump-polluted realized level for five of six names; only Nvidia is above, and that is earnings-driven. Nvidia's Nov 20 expiry IV of 72.2% versus 60.6% at 4 DTE is the expected event hump ahead of Nov 17; premium into this binary event is to be avoided. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names, no free IV-history source is available. 0-DTE IVs printed 1-11% after the close and are expiry-day artifacts, not vol readings. Put-call parity looks intact on the live chains (tight ATM call/put IVs at every non-0DTE expiry).
desks.Quant lab: Eight new candidates were scored and added to the ledger (#238-245), 4 WATCH, 4 ARCHIVE, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. #245 Strasmore Research SQL API (score 61, WATCH) is the first free, no-key SQL source of options IV and Greeks the lab has verified live: a demo query returned 5 real rows in 320 ms. The free tier is limited to 1 year of history, so it covers recent-window IV/Greeks work but not multi-year IV history, and the vendor declines written market-data-rights confirmations, so licensing diligence is owed before any desk reliance. #238 (end-of-day reversal replication, pre-registered, honest null windows) and #239 (RL execution-policy transfer) are WATCH for their validation discipline, not desk signals.

items.detail: Nvidia's board announced Sun Nov 8 an independent investigation, supported by outside legal counsel, into reports CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company states no reason to believe US national security or company secrets were compromised; the allegations, the investigation outcome, and the timeline are UNVERIFIED. The stock fell to $175.89 pre-market Monday and closed at $178.67, down 13.6% in four sessions from $206.69 on Nov 3. Earnings Tue Nov 17 after close (consensus $2.49, 13 estimates) now carry a governance overhang on top of the earnings binary. Options imply a move of about 9.6%, about 1.7 times the 5.8% average absolute reaction of the last three prints. The Nov 20 expiry IV of 72.2% versus 60.6% at 4 DTE is the expected event hump. Premium into the print is to be avoided.

Physical shipping has not normalized: a UKMTO-verified tanker fire and projectile strike Nov 7, a Houthi hit damaging the Aramco Tower Nov 8, and an attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline Nov 9 (operations unaffected). The market is pricing reduced near-term war-risk premium on diplomacy headlines, not a resolution of physical supply disruption. Catalysts: USDA WASDE Tue Nov 10, 12:00 ET, with soybeans the wildcard (ending-stocks survey spread 280-404 million bushels); EIA petroleum report Thu Nov 12, 12:00 ET, a Veterans Day delay, not Wed Nov 11.
items.title: Oil fell 3-4% on diplomacy headlines, but Hormuz shipping has not normalized

items.detail: Fed funds effective 3.88%, 2-year 4.51%, 10-year 4.86% (FRED, as of Fri Nov 6; Monday's prints not yet published). The 10-year is down about 45 bp from its Oct 5 peak of 5.31%. 2s10s is +35 bp, still upward sloping but flattening about 13 bp over the past month. SOFR minus effective fed funds is +1 bp, and overnight borrowing is at 3.88% across SOFR, EFFR, and OBFR: no funding stress. Long rates easing from early-October highs reduces discount-rate pressure on growth multiples, modestly supportive for the growth-heavy watchlist names; the 10-year at 4.86% remains elevated in absolute terms, so the pressure is lessened, not gone.
items.title: Rates are a mild tailwind; funding is calm
